name: Avoiding whispering
lead: Avoiding whispering is a voice-care habit in which a person speaks softly in a normal, voiced manner instead of whispering when trying to rest or protect the voice. It is discussed in appearance-related voice improvement as part of reducing vocal strain.

Phonetically, whispering is an unvoiced mode of speech in which the vocal folds are held apart and do not vibrate, while air turbulence between the arytenoid cartilages makes the sound.[1] Wikipedia notes that whispering can strain the vocal cords more than regular speech for some people, who are advised to speak softly instead, but sources this to a 2011 newspaper article rather than a medical study.[1]

Voice-therapy and vocal-hygiene literature summarised on Wikipedia lists reducing overall speech quantity, avoiding throat clearing and shouting, and staying hydrated, and does not specifically address whispering.[3]

paras: Proponents describe the practice as replacing whispered speech with quiet, easy, voiced speech during hoarseness or voice fatigue. Whispering is a distinct phonation mode with no standard IPA symbol, because no language uses it to distinguish words.[1]

The general sources reviewed here state that improper or prolonged talking can cause vocal loading and that repeated vocal abuse can produce nodules, and that hoarseness lasting more than two weeks should be medically evaluated.[2] Phonotrauma and habitual vocal hyperfunction are described as causes of vocal fold injury.[4]

The specific claim that whispering is harder on the folds than quiet voiced speech is described as applying to some people and rests on a press report in the cited encyclopedia entry; no controlled study is cited there.[1] Voice therapy is described as individualized, with no single method working for everyone.[3]
No studies found. Related research on vocal loading and voice therapy exists in clinical literature but was not located for whispering specifically.

card.summary: A voice-care habit of speaking softly instead of whispering; the claim rests on limited and indirect evidence.
card.note: Persistent hoarseness over two weeks is generally advised to be medically evaluated.

quick.overview:
Avoiding whispering means using quiet voiced speech rather than whispering when the voice is tired or hoarse. It is discussed as a vocal hygiene habit.

The claim that whispering strains the vocal cords is noted in reference works as applying to some people, and is sourced to a news article rather than a trial.
quick.mechanism: Whispering keeps the vocal folds apart and produces sound from air turbulence. Proponents say people often push harder to be heard, which may add strain; this mechanism was not tested in the sources reviewed.
quick.risks: Few risks are attached to the habit itself. Experts generally advise medical evaluation if hoarseness lasts more than two weeks.
